feature: A menu that says Custom lets you pick Custom
summary: Try a named spot or a preset size over a value of your own, and Custom in the same menu now gives your value back. It works the same way in a turn's Around menu, both Curve menus, and the size lists in New Frame, New Canvas and New Video.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its defaults. Walk: Scripts/playtest/custom-goes-back-walk.json.

try.do: Draw a tall rectangle, pick it, press the plus on the Motion header and choose Rotation.
Drag the crosshair labelled pivot to just above the shape. Around reads Custom.
Open the Around menu and choose Top centre. The shape now swings from its top edge.
Open Around again and choose Custom, below the line. Your own point is back, and At shows its numbers.
Choose Layer > New Frame, pick Custom and type 300 by 200, then click Desktop. The Custom row now shows 300 × 200.
Click Custom. The boxes read 300 and 200 again, and Add Frame makes that size.
Do the same in File > New Blank Canvas: type 640 by 480, click Square, click Custom.

evaluate: Is Custom below a line, under the three named spots, where you would look for your own point?
With a preset picked, does the size beside Custom in New Frame, New Canvas and New Video make it obvious that clicking Custom brings your size back?
Custom appears in Around only once you have had a point of your own. Is that right, or would you rather always see it, dimmed until there is one?
Your own pivot is saved with the document, so it is still there to pick after you reopen the file. Is that what you would expect?
rough: The two Curve menus (Motion's Curve, which says Drawn, and Properties' Between the keys Curve, which says Custom) offer the same way back, but no walk can draw a curve yet, so those two are checked only by unit tests and a build, not on screen.
The Properties curve remembers your drawn curve for as long as the window is open. The pivot and Motion's curve are saved with the document.

The mock ends the Around menu with Somewhere else (Y) and puts a move button beside it. The app has never had either, so that is filed as its own task: the-around-menu-ends-with-somewhere-else-as-the.
Custom does not carry a checkmark in Around or Motion's Curve, because no menu in the Motion section marks its current value. The Properties dropdown does mark it.
